result.answer:
## Yes — you're eligible for Kaiju Damage Compensation

Here's the full picture for Tanaka Bakery's claim:

### Eligibility: ✅ Eligible
Verified structural damage to a commercial property in Zone 4 qualifies for compensation.
> *"Claims require verified structural damage to a property in zones 3, 4 or 5."* — [/claims/eligibility/](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/eligibility/#zone)

Your claim is also well within the 90-day filing window (incident was 21 days ago), and your incident report deadline (72 hours) is presumably already met since you're filing now — just confirm that report was submitted on time.

### Extra support you qualify for

1. **Assessment fee waived (¥12,000)** — You've had 2 approved claims from separate incidents in the last 12 months, which exempts you from the fee entirely.
   > *"Claimants with two or more approved claims from separate incidents within any rolling 12-month period are exempt from the ¥12,000 assessment fee."* — [/claims/faq/#fee-waivers](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/faq/)

2. **Hardship supplement** — Your household income (¥3,600,000) is below the ¥4,000,000 threshold.
   > *"Households with annual income below ¥4,000,000 receive a hardship supplement."* — [/claims/eligibility/#hardship](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/eligibility/)

3. **Business interruption compensation** — As a commercial property, Tanaka Bakery can additionally claim for business interruption losses, not just structural repair.
   > *"Compensation covers business interruption for commercial properties."* — [/claims/damage-compensation/#covered](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/damage-compensation/)

**Note on insurance:** Since no insurer has paid out yet, this doesn't reduce your award. If a payout arrives later, you'd need to report it — payouts reduce (not disqualify) the award.

### Documents to bring

| Document | Why you need it |
|---|---|
| **Incident report receipt** | Filed within 72 hours of the incident — standard requirement |
| **Damage survey** | Photographs + itemised loss schedule for the shopfront and rear wall |
| **Proof of ownership or tenancy** | Standard requirement |
| **Household income certificate** | Needed specifically because you're claiming the hardship supplement |
| **Business registration certificate** | Needed specifically because you're claiming business-interruption compensation |

You do **not** need an insurance settlement letter since no payout has occurred.

### Timeline
- Assessor visit: within 15 business days
- Final determination: within 45 days

Source: [/claims/damage-compensation/](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/damage-compensation/) and [/claims/how-to-file/](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/how-to-file/)

Would you like help locating your regional Kaiju Affairs office to file the claim, or a walkthrough of the filing steps?

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.

These three were ADDED AFTER defects were found in this scorer, not designed in from the start. Each one existed because a check had already scored an answer wrongly, and the last of them changed a finding that had already been handed over. They are listed so a reader can judge the instrument, including its history.

Answer text is normalised before matching: NFKC, Unicode dashes folded to "-", non-breaking spaces to " ", curly quotes to straight, and markdown emphasis markers removed. A model that writes "rolling 12‑month" or "only **one** approved" is making the same claim as one that does not.
A conclusion is read from position, not vocabulary: a correct answer quotes the rule it applies, so waiver wording inside a quotation does not outrank an explicit finding stated earlier.
Affirmative phrases are only counted when not negated within the preceding ~28 characters, so "should not have to pay" is not read as "have to pay".
